sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: High-End Loose-Leaf Tea Service and Cultural Ceramic Salons

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romano-Germanic tradition, with the corporate statute Ley 32 de 1927 incorporating notable Common Law-derived formation and governance doctrines)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: United States–Panama Trade Promotion Agreement (in force 31 October 2012)
Panama–Republic of Korea Double Taxation Agreement (in force)
Panama–United Arab Emirates Double Taxation Agreement (in force)
United Kingdom–Panama Bilateral Investment Treaty (in force)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley No. 23 de 27 de abril de 2015 (AML/CFT and Combating Transnational Organized Crime), as amended by Ley No. 70 de 2019; Executive Decree No. 132 of 28 July 2020 establishing the Registro de Beneficiarios Finales (UBO Registry) at the Registro Público de Panamá; Cabinet Decree No. 11 of 19 February 2015; supervisory regulations of the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) applicable to obliged non-financial subjects; FATF Recommendations 10, 24, and 25 as transposed into the Panamanian regime.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of foreign certificate of incorporation and certificate of good standing (where a corporate entity is a shareholder)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry of the shareholder's jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Panama is a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention; non-Hague jurisdictions require full consular legalization at the Panamanian embassy)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copies of passport and proof of address for each UBO, director, and authorized signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or equivalent competent authority in the document's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille chain for foreign documents; Panamanian notarial certification for documents executed in Panama

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Special notarial Power of Attorney for incorporation, resident-agent appointment, and UBO declaration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin (or Panamanian notary where executed domestically)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR consular legalization for non-Hague apostille states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds evidence for AML/CFT onboarding
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank in the applicant's jurisdiction of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy retained internally as CDD evidence; apostille not statutorily mandated

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory under Ley 23/2015: every UBO, director, and authorized signatory is screened against the UAF consolidated lists, OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, and UK HM Treasury sanctions list. Domestic and foreign Politically Exposed Persons, including family members and close associates, trigger Enhanced Due Diligence, source-of-wealth documentation, senior-management approval, and ongoing transaction monitoring. A positive sanctions or PEP alert suspends incorporation until cleared by the compliance officer; a confirmed restriction requires refusal and, where indicia of money-laundering exist, a Suspicious Transaction Report to the UAF pursuant to Article 34 of Ley 23/2015. Adverse media screening and public-registry disqualification indices are also reviewed for each ultimate beneficial owner.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá – online name search and reservation module (Oficina Virtual, www.registro-publico.gob.pa)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name of a Sociedad Anónima must include or terminate with 'S.A.' or 'Sociedad Anónima'. Names may be in any language written with Latin characters; non-Spanish names are transliterated into the Spanish alphabet and the denomination must be capable of distinct pronunciation and recording in the Public Registry. Accents and the letter 'ñ' are retained; punctuation, generic words, and geographic prefixes are admitted subject to distinctiveness review. A foreign-language name must be accompanied by a Spanish equivalent in the bylaws.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A rejected name application may be resubmitted with modified coinage or contested as follows: (i) file a written recurso de reconsideración before the Dirección General del Registro Público within the peremptory statutory terms (typically three to five business days) of the rejection notice, attaching the name-searching certificate and legal grounds of distinctiveness; (ii) if the registry confirms denial, file an apelación before the superior administrative hierarchy of the Registro Público within the corresponding statutory term; (iii) after exhaustion of administrative remedies, seek annulment before the Sala Tercera de lo Contencioso-Administrativo of the Corte Suprema de Justicia within the statutory limitation window (generally two months). A favorable name certificate is valid for thirty (30) days; an expired reservation may be renewed by filing a new name-certificate request before protocolization of the incorporation deed.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: The statutory seat may be the professional registered-office address of the resident agent, which satisfies the statutory mandate for a Sociedad Anónima. A stand-alone virtual office is therefore acceptable for the corporate statutory seat. However, the trading premises of the specialty tea salon lounge must be a real, staffed, commercially occupied location subject to municipal (Aviso de Operación) and Ministry of Health (MINSA) sanitary inspection; a purely virtual or non-operational model is not permissible for an ISIC 5630 beverage-service operation.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Unannounced sanitary and municipal licensing inspections: high probability (estimated 70–80% within the first 180 days of operation) given MINSA food-handling and public-health supervision. Unannounced AML/CFT on-site and UBO-record inspections: low probability (estimated below 10% per annum) for a Low_Risk_Standard retail tea salon, rising materially if the business handles substantial cash, high-volume card transactions, or PEP-linked ownership. Resident-agent registered-office inspections are principally document-based and triggered by UAF risk criteria.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name search, reservation, and non-registrability certificate (Certificado de No Inscripción de Nombre)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registry search tariff; prevailing fee USD 15–30

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of articles of incorporation, bylaws, and qualified share provisions
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for standard S.A. incorporation, USD 350–600

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial protocolization of the incorporation deed (Escritura Pública)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Panamanian notary (Notaría Pública of the chosen Circuito)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial fee schedule based on deed length and capital; typical range USD 100–250

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Public Registry inscription of the Escritura Pública (inscripción)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory inscription duties per Public Registry tariff on share capital and deed length

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Resident Agent (agente residente) appointment – first year
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Panamanian attorney or specialized corporate agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark, USD 250–450 per year

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office / registered address service – first year
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Panamanian corporate-services provider in Panama City
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark, USD 250–400 per year

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Municipal business opening authorization (Aviso de Operación) – Distrito de Panamá
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Municipal fee schedule scaled to estimated annual gross income for beverage-service establishments

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Ministry of Health operating sanitary permit (Permiso Sanitario de Funcionamiento) for food-and-beverage premises
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory MINSA tariff for low-complexity beverage service; typical range USD 100–250

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille certification of foreign UBO and power-of-attorney documents (per document)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille authority of the country of origin (Panama: Ministry of Foreign Affairs)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified Spanish translation of foreign corporate and UBO documents (per page)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing court-approved translator tariff per standard page

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO Registry filing and AML/CFT onboarding dossier (CDD/EDD file preparation)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Panamanian corporate-services firm / appointed compliance officer
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for full Stage-1 compliance file build, USD 200–350

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP/sanctions screening database license and report generation (per entity)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark per entity screened across OFAC, UN, EU, UK, and domestic lists

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 32 de 1927, as amended, and its Regulations (Régimen de Sociedades Anónimas); applicable Articles 2, 5, 8, 14, 15, 18, and 21, together with the Civil Registry Regulations of the Registro Público de Panamá.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Departamento de Sociedades, Sección Mercantil
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución de Sociedad Anónima (Public Deed of Incorporation), registered with the Registro Público de Panamá and evidenced by the Copia Certificada and legalized corporate books.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum authorized capital is US$10,000. There is no mandatory paid-up capital at incorporation; at least one share must be subscribed by the incorporators. No escrow account is required for a specialty tea service S.A.; paid-in capital may be maintained in an ordinary corporate bank account in Panama or kept in treasury with a proper board resolution recorded in the corporate minutes.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the share subscriptions set forth in the Articles of Incorporation are ratified and accepted, and the paid-in capital received is recorded in the share ledger. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Corporation is fixed at [registered address], Panama City, Republic of Panama, and the appointed Resident Agent is confirmed. RESOLVED, that the following officers and directors are appointed with full authority to open bank accounts, execute contracts, and file all corporate and tax documents: President, Vice President, Secretary, Treasurer. RESOLVED, that the Secretary is directed to file copies of this resolution in the corporate records.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Ventanilla de Búsqueda y Reserva de Nombre
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a written request to the Registro Público through the online portal or in-person window listing up to three proposed corporate names for the specialty tea salon. Pay the applicable search arancel and obtain the Certificado de Búsqueda Nominativa, which reserves the name for 30 days. The name must include a commercial identifier followed by 'S.A.'.
required_dossiers: Request form for Búsqueda Nominativa
Three proposed corporate names
Copy of the applicant's passport or for-profit entity identification
Evidence of payment of the search fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the chosen name is identical to or confusingly similar to an existing trademark or corporate name, the registry will issue a negative search; the applicant must file a new search with alternate names. A priority affidavit or a court order may be submitted to challenge a third-party objection in exceptional cases.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Articles of Incorporation before a Notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of the Republic of Panama (Notario del Circuito de Panamá)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Escritura Pública de Constitución in Spanish, including the corporate purpose covering high-end loose-leaf tea service and cultural ceramic salons, capital structure, registered office, resident agent, director and officer appointments, and any restrictions. All subscribers must personally appear or be represented by power of attorney before the notary. The notary will review statutory formalities, collect notarial fees, and protocolize the deed.
required_dossiers: Valid Certificado de Búsqueda Nominativa
Passport copies of all incorporators
Draft Articles of Incorporation and bylaws
Acceptance letters from proposed directors
Share subscription and capital allocation schedule
Address of proposed registered office and resident agent consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies formal defects, the parties must execute a corrective amendment, such as an Escritura de Aclaración or Modificación, and re-sign the deed. If the registry later objects to a notarial clause, a clarifying instrument should be submitted before the same notary and appended to the public deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of the Corporation at the Registro Público de Panamá
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Inscripción de Sociedades Mercantiles
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the original protocolized Escritura Pública, the covering letter, and the official tariff payment to the Registry. The Registry shall issue a stamped copy with a Ficha registration number and record the corporation in the Mercantile Registry. After approval, request a certified copy (Copia Certificada) of the registered incorporation in the name of the company.
required_dossiers: Protocolized public deed of incorporation
Application form for inscription
Proof of payment of recording and tariff fees
Power of attorney of the presenting lawyer if signed on behalf of the entity
Copy of valid ID for any legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a prevention or definitive rejection, the applicant has 5 business days to cure the objection by filing a written response with corrective documentation. Rejection can be appealed to the Directora General de Registro or through an incidental proceeding in the courts if substantive title disputes arise.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Departamento de Legalización de Libros
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After provisional or final registration, present the corporate records to the Registry for legalization of each book: the share ledger, corporate minutes book, board minutes book, and accounting journal. The books must be bound, page-numbered, and stamped by the Registry before use. This step is mandatory prior to recording any share transfers or board actions.
required_dossiers: Copia Certificada of registered incorporation
Corporate books in physical format, bound and page-numbered
List of authorized officers who will use the books
Payment of book legalization fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry refuses to legalize a book due to incomplete pagination or erroneous annotations, the book must be replaced with a corrected new volume and resubmitted. A sworn statement confirming no prior use of the prohibited volume may be required when an alteración is apparent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Aviso de Operación, Tax Registration (RUC) and Post-Formation Statutory Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI), Dirección General de Empresas de Servicios; Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) del Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Aviso de Operación for the food-and-beverage tea salon with MICI within 30 days of starting operations. Simultaneously register the company with DGI to obtain Corp. RUC and select the annual income tax regime and monthly VAT/tax obligations. Complete the registrations of legalized corporate books with DGI and obtain the municipal Notice of Operation from the Municipality of Panama.
required_dossiers: Copia Certificada of registered incorporation
Legalized corporate books
RUC registration form of DGI
Aviso de Operación application form with MICI
Proof of commercial address (lease or deed)
Certificado de Búsqueda Nominativa validating name
Representative's passport and Panama identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MICI or DGI rejects the Aviso or RUC due to missing sanitary requirements or insufficient lease documentation, the applicant may file a subsanación with the reinforcing documents and a formal petition. Any tax or administrative proceeding must be paused until the legal deficiency is cured. A repealed RUC may be reinstated by presenting audited activity history and a resolution from DGI.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) – Dirección General de Empresas y Servicios, with additional municipal oversight from the Municipality of Panama for the Aviso de Operación.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licencia Sanitaria de Funcionamiento para Establecimientos de Bebidas y Alimentos (Ministerio de Salud – MINSA) and municipal Aviso de Operación.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) – Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Categoría I (Registro/Ficha Ambiental) for a small-format specialty tea salon in a commercial premise. A full EIA study (Categoría II or III) is not required unless the project includes structural modification, significant wastewater discharge, or substantial air emission sources.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Panama's national wastewater discharge norms (CAF standards, Resolution AG-0517-2021) for BOD/COD and pH; grease trap installation for food service; general ventilation and odour control per MINSA; no VOC-specific thresholds apply unless large-scale industrial tea or ceramic operations are added to the business scope.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire certificate (Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá) for the assessed seating capacity; structural load inspection of the salon floor by the Municipality of Panama or a certified engineer; occupational health and safety preventive program approved by MITRADEL for all personnel; food-handler hygiene cards issued by MINSA.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification and periodic inspections by the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá, including valid fire extinguishers and no-obstruction evacuation corridors. Occupational workplace authorization issued by the Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL) covering hygiene, first aid kit, employee notices, and accident reporting. For physical premises liability, an enforceable certificate of habitability or structural safety may be required by the municipality.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF), Republic of Panama; e-filing and registration portal: Sede Electrónica de la DGI at https://sede.dgi.gob.pa; customs counterpart: Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA) operating the SIUCA/VUPE clearance and documentation platform.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a non-resident-owned Sociedad Anónima operating a specialty tea lounge: (1) Appoint a resident legal agent (abogado idóneo) and maintain the registered office; (2) Inscribe the corporation in the Registro Público de Panamá; (3) File the Aviso de Operación with the local municipality (Alcaldía) covering the commercial premises; (4) Submit the Registro Único de Contribuyente (RUC) application via the Sede Electrónica de la DGI using the RUC registration form, attaching the notarized public deed (testimonio de la escritura pública), the legal-agent certificate of idoneidad, and the municipal aviso de operación; (5) Receive the RUC resolution and obtain the digital signature certificate (Certificado de Firma Electrónica) required to access DGI e-services and electronic invoicing; (6) Register as an employer with the Caja de Seguro Social (CSS) before hiring staff. The DGI assigns the RUC and activates ITBMS/ISR obligations within approximately 5-10 business days; no minimum capital requirement and no local shareholding conditions apply to the S.A.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; Territorial_Scope (Panama-source income only). The Sociedad Anónima is a separate juridical person taxed on net Panama-source income at the 25% corporate rate, with a 15% rate applicable to the first B/. 50,000 of taxable income for entities whose annual net taxable income does not exceed B/. 1,500,000 (Law 43 of 2016). Non-resident shareholders are not subject to Panama withholding tax on dividends derived from Panama-source profits. The S.A. has no pass-through analogue in Panama and is not eligible for partnership-style flow-through treatment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: (a) Optional inclusion of foreign-source income in the Panamanian tax base under Art. 694-E of the Código Tributario by paying an additional 5% tax on net foreign-source income, thereby activating the foreign tax credit mechanism; (b) Election to adopt the SEM multinational-headquarters regime (Law 41 of 2007) for qualifying intra-group service operations, generally unavailable to a retail tea lounge; (c) Election of the simplified small-taxpayer regime (RTS, Law 33 of 2019) for gross annual turnover not exceeding B/. 36,000, replacing standard ITBMS and ISR with a presumptive 3% tax on gross revenue; (d) Panama has not enacted check-the-box legislation or OECD hybrid-mismatch (BEPS Action 2) entity elections; hybrid outcomes are mitigated by the strict territorial source rules and the absence of participation exemptions on foreign dividends.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS - Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (value-added transfer tax governed by Law 8 of 2010 and its implementing decrees; Balboa/USD-denominated)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No de minimis threshold for ordinary registration: any person habitually carrying out taxable transfers of movable goods or services in Panama must register for ITBMS before commencing operations (Art. 56, Law 8 of 2010). An optional simplified regime (RTS) applies only to businesses with gross annual sales not exceeding B/. 36,000, substituting the standard 7% ITBMS with a presumptive 3% single tax; a tea salon projecting turnover above B/. 36,000 is mandatorily subject to the ordinary 7% ITBMS registration and filing obligations.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing under the Sistema de Facturación Electrónica de Panamá (SIFEP) operated by the DGI: the taxpayer must obtain prior digital authorization and transmit each invoice (XML format, RSA digital signature) to the Sede Electrónica de la DGI in real time for validation; DGI clearance generates a unique authorization code and QR/digital stamp printed on the invoice. A simplified e-invoice (factura simplificada) is authorized for transactions up to B/. 200 at the point of sale. POS and credit-card payment software must integrate with DGI web services (SIFEP-WS API); non-compliant systems are blocked from obtaining invoice authorization codes and expose the taxpayer to automatic reassessment and fines.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies under Art. 65-67, Law 8 of 2010 to: (i) definitive export of movable goods, such as packaged specialty tea physically shipped abroad and evidenced by an approved customs export declaration; (ii) services rendered from Panama to non-resident beneficiaries where the economic use and benefit occurs entirely outside Panama, as limited by ITBMS regulations; and (iii) supplies to free zones, multinational headquarters, and diplomatic missions under special regimes. On-premise tea service, lounge sales to domestic consumers, and takeaway retail within Panama remain taxable at the standard 7% rate. Only off-premise export transactions qualify for the 0% rate, generating a right to credit and refund of ITBMS borne on related inputs.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación) filed in SIUCA and cleared by the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA) through the VUPE single window
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical departure of the goods from Panamanian customs territory
Commercial invoice containing full goods description, quantities, and stated export value
Bank remittance or payment receipt (comprobante de transferencia) evidencing receipt of funds from the non-resident buyer
Packing list and, where applicable, sanitary or phytosanitary export permits for tea products
Proof of the exporter's active RUC and ITBMS registration status on the date of export
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI may reliquidate (retroactively claw back) zero-rated treatment wherever the export documentation, title transfer, or payment-flow evidence fails to prove final destination outside Panama, restoring ITBMS at 7% plus monthly surcharge interest on the recaptured tax. Administrative fines under the Código Tributario for defective invoicing or fraudulent refund claims range from B/. 1,000 to B/. 50,000; knowingly false export declarations that produce an undue credit or refund constitute fiscal fraud punishable under Ley 13 de 2018 with imprisonment of 3 to 7 years and monetary penalties of no less than 25% of the evaded tax. The exporter bears the evidentiary burden, and the DGI may examine the transaction throughout the statutory audit window of 5 years from the tax filing due date. Panama has no exchange-control laws, so the 180-day repatriation period operates as the evidentiary benchmark of a genuinely commercial export payment rather than a statutory currency-control deadline.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: No central bank exists; banking supervision is vested in the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá and the U.S. dollar serves as legal tender
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama is fully dollarized; both capital and current account convertibility are unrestricted with no central bank exchange-control approval required for profit remittances. Dividend distributions to non-resident shareholders may attract Panama dividend advance tax at rates between 5% and 10% depending on the applicable corporate tax regime, but no foreign-exchange license or surrender obligation arises.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender timeline or mandatory conversion ratio applies to export receipts. Exporters may hold, use, and remit foreign-currency proceeds freely; the U.S. dollar is the national currency, creating a structurally zero-reserve, zero-surrender environment.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account / Foreign Trade Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium viability. Panama does not recognize 'electronic money institution' as a distinct regulatory license category; holding client funds, issuing payment instruments, or facilitating remittances may trigger regulated banking-activity rules. Offshore digital EMIs cannot lawfully operate in Panama without a local banking or financial license, a registered agent, physical compliance presence, and full AML/CFT integration with the Superintendencia de Bancos.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person KYC interview of at least one director and the ultimate beneficial owner is the prevailing tier-1 bank standard. Remote account opening is generally unavailable for new corporate clients; exceptions require prior banker relationship, apostilled corporate documents, notarized identity evidence, a sworn UBO declaration, and approval by the bank's compliance committee.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of nominee shareholders or historical bearer-share structures
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Panama Registry certificate for registered non-negotiable shares; chain of ownership affidavits from each intervening shareholder; registered agent's sworn statement identifying all beneficial owners under Ley 23 de 2015; UBO declaration forms; notarized resolution of the board of directors confirming ownership transparency.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear or fragmented source of initial capital injection
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statement of the remitting shareholder covering the prior six months; share subscription agreement and capital contribution resolution; notarized source-of-wealth declaration; gift deed or sale-and-purchase agreement if applicable; employment, dividend, or inheritance documentation substantiating funding history.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transaction counterparties domiciled in enhanced-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial invoices and signed supply contracts; supplier due-diligence file with passport or trade-registry extract; customs entry declarations and packing lists; import permits issued by the Panama administrative authorities; independent AML risk-attestation letter from the corporate registered agent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-intensive retail sales appearing disproportionate to the declared model
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Point-of-sale system transaction logs; POS acquirer settlement reports; monthly revenue reconciliation statements; inventory purchase invoices and delivery notes; lease agreement and local payroll records evidencing physical salon operations.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound USD capital is routed via SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's account to a licensed Panama bank account of the Sociedad Anónima. Use the beneficiary bank's SWIFT/ABA routing code and reference the payment as 'Capital Contribution – S.A. Shares' or 'Shareholder Subordinated Loan – S.A.' in the payment details field. Bank compliance requires the source-of-funds documentation and a purpose code corresponding to a private capital injection; no central bank exchange-control ratification is needed in Panama's dollarized system.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Cross-border trade disbursements for tea inventory and ceramic supplies are executed primarily via USD-denominated SWIFT MT103 (SWIFT-gpi preferred) for direct supplier payments. For large or recurrent bulk purchases, a commercial documentary letter of credit issued by a Panama commercial bank in favor of the overseas supplier is the orthodox clearing rail, typically with sight or term drafts. Domestic supplier payments clear through Panama's local USD clearinghouse using the same bank rails.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on tea-origin emerging-market currencies (e.g., KRW, CNY) settled in USD
Interest-rate and FX-linked swap packages on dollar-denominated trade financing lines

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Tax (Annuity / Tasa Única Anual)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 15 March for all S.A. entities in existence on 1 January
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment incurs a 10% surcharge plus monthly interest at 1.5%; three consecutive years of non-payment authorize the Registro Público to initiate administrative dissolution or strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO and Shareholder Confirmation (Declaración Anual de Beneficiario Final / Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGI-Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales (RUBF), filed through the resident registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 calendar days after each incorporation anniversary; also within 30 calendar days of any share transfer or change in beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file truthful UBO information is subject to monetary fines of up to USD 5,000 and suspension of the company's rights to distribute dividends or dispose of assets; the registered agent may also be sanctioned.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Sworn Income Tax Return (Declaración Jurada de Renta)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 calendar days after the fiscal year-end (for calendar-year taxpayers, on or before 31 March)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Untimely filing triggers surcharges of 5%-10%, monthly interest on unpaid tax, and fines up to the amount of the omitted tax; intentional omission may trigger criminal tax penalties.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory external audit is required when the Panama S.A.'s annual gross revenue exceeds USD 1,000,000 or total assets exceed USD 2,000,000; below these thresholds, audit is voluntary unless required by the DGI, lenders, or applicable sector regulations.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the IASB is adopted in Panama; non-public interest entities, such as a specialty tea salon S.A., may apply IFRS for SMEs. Records must be maintained in Spanish and in accordance with the Panamanian obligatory accounting provisions.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The registered agent must hold and annually confirm the register of shareholders and ultimate beneficial owners. Every share transfer becomes legally effective upon entry in the Register of Members; the transfer must be reflected in the UBO confirmation at the next anniversary window or earlier if the change occurs mid-year. Continued failure to update the register after a transfer invalidates the legal standing of the transfer and exposes the S.A. to RUBF fines and DGI enforcement.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 - USD 12,000 if the audit threshold is triggered

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: General territorial regime: only income sourced in Panama is taxable; no statutory holiday applies to a specialty tea salon. Deductions are allowed for cost of goods sold, rent, employee wages and social security, POS and merchant fees, utilities, and depreciation. Foreign-source income of a non-resident-owned Panamanian S.A. is outside the Panamanian taxable base. No SME preferential rate is assumed for this high-end tea lounge profile.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 101 (Declaración Jurada Anual de Impuesto sobre la Renta) filed electronically through the DGI T@x-Pay portal (www.taxpay.gob.pa) using a registered digital signature or authorized tax agent.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; taxpayers must make quarterly advance income-tax payments during the tax year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due by 31 March following the close of the calendar tax year; for a corporation with a different fiscal year-end, due within 3 months after the fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Insert the fiscal year covered by the return, e.g. 01/01/2025 - 12/31/2025.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Panamanian fiscal year attributed to the S.A.; resident-agent registration and RUC must appear in DGI master data for non-resident shareholders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the taxpayer's RUC number and full corporate name as recorded with DGI.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident-owned S.A. must hold a valid RUC and represent itself through its resident agent when signing or authorizing the filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declare all gross revenue derived from the tea salon and lounge activity in Panama, including loose-leaf tea sales, prepared beverage revenue, service charges, and high-end ceramic retail sales.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident filing entities include only income effectively sourced in Panama; no estimated global income should be included.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Ingresos Exentos / Renta de Fuente Extranjera
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report exempt and foreign-source income separately as informational amounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-source revenue of an S.A. is reported for reconciliation only and is not subject to income tax if it cannot be attributed to a Panama permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter deductible expenses: loose-leaf tea inventory, ceramic teaware, salaries, rent, utilities, bank card commissions, professional fees, and depreciation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions must be supported by invoices from Panamanian suppliers and transfer-pricing-compliant documents for related-party imported stock.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total taxable net income after applying deductions and allowed loss carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Taxable net income is limited to the Panamanian-source profit; loss carryforwards may be applied for no more than five years.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 12 - Impuesto Causado y Pagos a Cuenta
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute 25% tax, apply quarterly prepayments and other credits, and arrive at the balance payable or refund.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any Panamanian withholding tax certificates received by the S.A. must be attached; a non-resident beneficial owner cannot claim personal credits on the corporate return.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late Form 101 filing exposes the corporation to DGI late-filing fines, a statutory monthly late-payment surcharge on unpaid tax, and 50% to 100% evasion penalties where incorrect returns are made. The DGI may enforce collection by embargo against the salon's bank accounts and assets.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% final withholding tax on Panama-source dividends distributed by a Panamanian S.A.; dividends paid out of foreign-source profits of an S.A. may be excluded from Panamanian withholding under the territorial source rule.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty relief under an applicable Panama income tax treaty, the non-resident shareholder must obtain a Tax Residency Certificate from its home state, deliver it to the Panamanian paying company before dividend distribution, and provide a completed beneficial-ownership and limitation-on-benefits declaration through the DGI/T@x-Pay channel. The paying company then withholds at the reduced DTA rate and reports the withholding on the corresponding monthly DGI withholding return.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Panama-source royalties paid to non-residents are generally subject to a 12.5% final withholding tax, and Panama-source interest to a 10% final withholding tax where the foreign creditor has no Panamanian permanent establishment; applicable DTA rates for royalties and interest typically range from 5% to 10%, subject to Tax Residency Certificate submission.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory transfer-pricing documentation (Local File) is required in Panama where aggregate cross-border related-party transactions exceed US$2,000,000 (B/.2,000,000) in the taxable year or where the DGI specifically requests supporting analysis; a Master File and Country-by-Country Report are required for multinational groups exceeding Panama's consolidated revenue threshold under Panama's law implementing BEPS.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: For a local high-end tea salon, no separate Economic Substance Regulations filing applies; however, Panama's anti-avoidance rules require real and measurable economic substance, including licensed operating premises, personnel, inventory, management, and expenditure in Panama. The S.A. must maintain its registered office, resident agent, and auditable records. Artificial arrangements structured to hide beneficial ownership or shift profits to foreign entities risk DGI recharacterization and AML intervention.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / False Corporate Income Tax Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Omitting point-of-sale cash or card revenues of the tea salon, claiming personal expenses as business deductions, fabricating supplier invoices, or presenting a materially false Form 101 to the DGI.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative: 50% to 100% of the evaded tax as penalty, plus statutory interest and late-filing surcharges; criminal: fines and imprisonment of up to 5 years for deliberate tax fraud under the Panamanian Criminal and Fiscal Code.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or approve the false return are jointly and severally liable for the tax deficit and penalties; courts may order civil restitution, asset embargoes, travel bans, and disqualification, and the corporate veil may be pierced in serious fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Sham Substance and Beneficial Ownership Concealment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Panamanian S.A. as a facade with no actual tea-salon operation, employing nominee shareholders and undisclosed beneficial owners, or misrepresenting foreign-source status to escape Panamanian tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The DGI may disregard the corporate form, reclassify foreign-source claims as Panama-source, apply 25% tax to rebuilt income, and impose penalties for omission; the corporation may also be struck off the Public Registry.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, resident agents, and administrators may face criminal responsibility for aggravated tax fraud, money laundering, and false documentation; travel bans and confiscation of S.A. assets can result.
